name: token_bonding_curves
description: Missing slippage protection in bonding-curve buy/sell functions enabling front-running/sandwich attacks
question: The source file in `source` implements a bonding-curve token contract with buy and/or sell functions that compute cost or proceeds from a supply-dependent price curve and transfer ETH/tokens, but at least one of these functions executes the trade without a caller-supplied slippage bound (e.g., no maximum acceptable cost on buy or minimum acceptable proceeds on sell) checked against the curve-computed value before minting/burning and transferring funds, allowing an attacker to front-run or sandwich the trade to profit at the trader's expense.
criteria: buy() computes getBuyCost/priceAtSupply and mints tokens without a maxCost or maxPayment parameter bounding acceptable price impact
sell() computes getSellProceeds and burns tokens/transfers ETH without a minProceeds or minReturn parameter
No require() comparing the curve-computed cost/proceeds against a caller-provided bound before executing mint/burn and transfer
Function parameter intended for slippage control (e.g., minTokens) is instead used as the exact trade amount rather than a bound check
Bonding curve buy/sell logic present with no commit-reveal or slippage-tolerance mechanism anywhere in the file
